sections.heading: Learning Point 1
sections.content: 1 India and the World: Land and the People 1 – The Story of Indian Farming The Story of Indian Farming CHAPTER 1 A farmer who looks after the welfare of his cattle, visits his farms daily, has the knowledge of the seasons, is careful about seeds, and is industrious, is rewarded with harvests of all kinds and never perishes.

sections.heading: Learning Point 6
sections.content: 2 Exploring Society: India and Beyond | Grade 7 Part 2 India’s Agricultural Landscape Farming or agriculture is one of the oldest occupations of humankind.

sections.heading: Learning Point 7
sections.content: It encompasses the preparation of soil, cultivation of plants, rearing of livestock, and, in many cases, the growing of trees as part of a comprehensive farming system.

sections.heading: Learning Point 8
sections.content: In some areas, farmers also practice pisciculture (fish rearing) or rear cocoons to extract silk thread.

sections.heading: Learning Point 9
sections.content: Very broadly, the term ‘agriculture’ encompasses farming, animal husbandry (raising livestock), forestry, and horticulture.

sections.heading: Learning Point 10
sections.content: DON’T MISS OUT The word agriculture comes from Latin.

sections.heading: Learning Point 11
sections.content: Agri means field and culture means to cultivate.

sections.heading: Learning Point 12
sections.content: The Government of India classifies economic activities related to agriculture as ‘agriculture and allied activities’.
sections.source_evidence: The Government of India classifies economic activities related to agriculture as ‘agriculture and allied activities’.

sections.heading: Learning Point 13
sections.content: Broadly, this includes agriculture, livestock- related activities, beekeeping (apiculture), fisheries, rearing of silkworms and preparing silk yarn, and fibre production, such as cotton and hemp.

sections.heading: Learning Point 14
sections.content: A little over 18 per cent of the country’s total value of goods and services produced in a year (gross domestic product) comes from agriculture and allied activities (2022-2023).

sections.heading: Learning Point 15
sections.content: Approximately 46 per cent of India’s working population is engaged in agriculture and allied activities for their livelihood (2022-2023).
sections.source_evidence: Approximately 46 per cent of India’s working population is engaged in agriculture and allied activities for their livelihood (2022-2023).

sections.heading: Learning Point 16
sections.content: A large proportion of families in India are closely connected to the land in one way or another, and in many cases, have been cultivating it for generations.

sections.heading: Learning Point 17
sections.content: Farming activities are, of course, essential for nurturing and sustaining the human population.

sections.heading: Learning Point 18

sections.heading: Learning Point 19
sections.content: However, in rural areas of India, more than 75 per cent of people working in the agriculture sector are women (2025).
